emergence.summary: A single-gene NPC1 loss-of-function. NPC1 encodes a large polytopic late-endosomal/lysosomal membrane protein that, with the soluble luminal partner NPC2, EXPORTS unesterified cholesterol (delivered by LDL endocytosis) out of the late endosome/lysosome and coordinates lysosomal sphingolipid trafficking. NPC1 LOF disables this export -> unesterified cholesterol, glycosphingolipids and sphingosine ACCUMULATE in late endosomes/lysosomes of neurons and viscera -> a neurovisceral disease: hepatosplenomegaly, progressive cerebellar ataxia, dystonia, dysphagia, cognitive decline and the characteristic VERTICAL SUPRANUCLEAR GAZE PALSY (the NPC spectrum, from neonatal cholestasis to adult neurodegeneration). The stored-lysosomal-load axis is driven UP by loss of the export 'brake'. This is read on the kit's lysosomal-storage axis -- the SEVENTH lysosomal read -- but as a TRAFFICKING / TRANSPORT defect, NOT a catabolic-enzyme defect: it is the explicit contrast both to the enzyme-replacement lysosomal reads (Gaucher, Fabry, Pompe, LIPA -- a missing catalyst) AND to cystinosis on a DIFFERENT cargo (cystinosis loses a lysosomal cystine EXPORTER; NPC loses a lysosomal cholesterol/sphingolipid EXPORTER -- both transport defects, corrected by lowering the stored substrate rather than by replacing an enzyme). The kit re-derives the approved restrain arm: SUBSTRATE REDUCTION -- miglustat, a glucosylceramide-synthase inhibitor that lowers glycosphingolipid synthesis so less accumulates (EMA-approved for NPC neurological manifestations) -- with arimoclomol, a heat-shock-response co-inducer that enhances lysosomal protein handling/function (FDA 2024 for NPC, used with miglustat), as the established adjunct correcting lysosomal function. (Levacetylleucine, approved 2024 for NPC neurological symptoms, is a further symptomatic adjunct.) The gamma read is of the NPC1 locus switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding/missense (notably the common p.Ile1061Thr allele), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].

per_gene.note: NPC1 encodes the late-endosomal/lysosomal membrane protein that, with NPC2, exports unesterified cholesterol (and coordinates sphingolipid trafficking) OUT of the lysosome -- functionally the EXPORT BRAKE on lysosomal lipid accumulation. LOF disables export -> cholesterol, glycosphingolipids and sphingosine accumulate in lysosomes of neurons and viscera. As a lost export 'brake' the stored-load axis goes UP (the same released-brake convention used for the cystinosis lysosomal transporter and for tyrosinaemia/haemochromatosis accumulation). Autosomal recessive, 18q11.2 (OMIM 607623). NCBI official symbol NPC1. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; the coding/missense lesions (e.g. p.Ile1061Thr) are outside the promoter firewall.

falsifiers.claim: NPC1 LOF (loss of the lysosomal cholesterol-export brake) raises stored lysosomal lipid load (axis UP)
falsifiers.falsifier: an NPC1 LOF allele that LOWERED lysosomal unesterified-cholesterol / glycosphingolipid storage would refute the lost-export-brake direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: filipin staining of lysosomal unesterified cholesterol and lysosomal glycosphingolipid content in NPC1-deficient vs control cells

falsifiers.claim: lowering the stored substrate (substrate reduction / enhanced lysosomal handling) is the CORRECTIVE direction
falsifiers.falsifier: if miglustat substrate reduction or arimoclomol RAISED stored lysosomal lipid or accelerated the neurological decline, the restrain/correct lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: lysosomal lipid content and neurological progression markers on substrate reduction / HSP co-induction in NPC models / patients
